jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Dorm Diplomacy
jokes.joke: I lived in a dorm with a guy who wanted to be a diplomat, so every roommate argument became a peace summit. I’d say, “Whose moldy ramen is this?” and he’d go, “Before assigning blame, we should recognize the legitimate security concerns of both bowls.” By finals week, our mini-fridge had sanctions.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Home Invasion
jokes.joke: My dorm room got broken into freshman year. Nothing stolen. Instead, my laundry was folded, my desk was alphabetized, and there was a Tupperware of lasagna in a mini-fridge that had never seen food before. I called campus security panicking. They ran it and said, 'Ma'am, that's not a break-in, that's just your mother with a spare key.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Negotiation Skills
jokes.joke: In college, I lived in a tiny dorm room with a guy who refused to wear headphones. I tried resolving it like a seasoned diplomat: careful negotiations, listening to his grievances, establishing neutral ground. That failed completely, so I switched to aggressive sanctions and hid his deodorant until he learned how Bluetooth works.

jokes.title: Campus Security Call
jokes.joke: I got back to my dorm room last week and realized there’d been a break-in. Door half open, drawers dumped, clothes everywhere. I freak out and call campus security. Two guys show up, take one look around, and the older one just sighs, ‘Sir… this is a dorm room. You’re fine.’

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Teenage Negotiations
jokes.joke: My parents said, “You’re a young adult now, start acting mature.” So I became the family diplomat. I’d negotiate curfews, Wi‑Fi passwords, laundry schedules. One night I proudly announced, “We’ve reached a compromise.” My dad goes, “Yeah, we all agreed you’re wrong, but you can present it in a PowerPoint.”

scores.comment: Strong escalation through increasingly suspicious acts of tidiness, with a clean mother reveal. The spare-key explanation is somewhat foreseeable but lands well.
Clear diplomat-to-sanctions structure and a solid final image, but the sanctions metaphor is the obvious comic route and hiding deodorant is only a mild payoff.
Cleanly written and immediately understandable, but the 'crime scene is actually normal dorm mess' reversal is familiar and offers only a moderate laugh.
Natural first-person setup and a decent parental reversal. The PowerPoint tag adds texture, but the underlying 'family unanimously says you're wrong' punchline is fairly conventional.
Solid escalation with a tight closing pun on 'sanctions'; clean voice and timing.
Familiar diplomat-roommate setup; ending is fine but less sharp than the sanctions callback in similar entries.
Relatable, economical, and the security guard's deadpan 'you're fine' lands cleanly.
Fresh family-negotiation angle; dad's PowerPoint line is a genuine non-obvious snap.
Solid escalation and comedic premise. The dialogue line about security concerns lands well, though the punchline about mini-fridge sanctions is slightly predictable once the bit is established.
Clean setup and believable details, but the 'mom secretly cleaned your messy room' turn is a very familiar sitcom/stand-up trope that softens the punchline.
Competent stage cadence, but the core premise—mistaking normal dorm room clutter for a burglary—is an ancient premise with no fresh spin on the finish.
A bit mild and generic family humor. The PowerPoint punchline feels tacked on rather than an organic, high-impact topper to the diplomat conceit.
